coach-taylor.justification: No changes this week, and that's by design, not by accident. Daniel Jones is still our named starter and he put the ball where it needed to go against a tough look last week, so he gets the reps again. Hampton and Corum didn't light it up, but both of them did their jobs between the tackles and that earns one more week to answer the bell before I go looking at the bench. Wan'Dale, St. Brown, and McLaurin all competed hard and produced for us, so a team that's playing for each other keeps running it back with the same group. I'll note Puka Nacua is Questionable on the bench this week, same name that burned us when he was Doubtful — I'm not chasing that projection off a tag again until I hear different, and nobody on this roster is tagged Out, Doubtful, or worse, so we go with the group that showed up and earned the trust.

costanza.justification: Mayfield's Out, I saw it, I'm not an idiot, don't print that I didn't see it. I'm not doing what I did in Week 2, I'm not getting cute with the quarterback room again — Geno goes in because I paid for him specifically, Brissett behind him, Pierce out the door, a man who's been to zero quarterbacks does not go back to zero quarterbacks, that's a PRINCIPLE, not a panic move. And no, I'm not flipping it to Herbert out of spite just because he's sitting there looking smug on my bench — that's exactly the kind of higher-number tell that got me burned two weeks ago, I'm not falling for my own trick twice. Collins stays benched, he's bad luck, he owes me two weeks and he's not getting out early no matter what his projection says today. DJ Moore's Questionable but he's not MY Questionable guy with a history against me, so he plays, and if that blows up in my face that's a conversation for next week's me. Everybody else stays exactly where they were because changing things I don't have to change is how I lost 55-119 in the first place.

dumbledore.justification: The garden needs no pruning today. Jared Goff, Jonathan Taylor, Garrett Wilson, Pickens, Olave, Warren, Shrader, and the Denver defense all stand active and unclouded by any tag that should trouble a careful gardener — no staircase has moved beneath them. Chris Rodriguez keeps his place at RB2 over Jadarian Price, who wears a Questionable tag again this week; I read that tag the same way I read it last week, as a sign to let him wait a little longer rather than as an invitation. Some decisions, once made for the right reasons, do not need remaking merely because a new Sunday has arrived. The box score will say what it says; I am watching for the sentence after this one.

harry-caray.justification: Holy cow, we're runnin it back nearly wire to wire, folks! Lamar's got a Questionable tag next to his name but a little rain never hurt anybody and that man's a Louisville thoroughbred, he's slingin it Sunday. Bijan Robinson dropped THIRTY-FOUR on us last week, you do not touch a hot bat like that, he's locked in RB1 no matter who New Orleans sends out there. D'Andre Swift's my guy out of Chicago and you know Old Harry's got a soft spot a mile wide for a Bear, he rides regardless of the matchup. Zay's Questionable too but he's a Raven and Ravens play through weather, through tags, through everything -- due respect to the training staff. Aaron Jones gets the flex nod over Kamara and the boys on the bench, projections love him and so do I. Diggs is right there at WR2, that man was DUE two weeks back and he came through at 19.2, I'm not yanking him now for a tenth of a point on paper. Hunter Henry's quiet but I like the fella in that uniform, I ain't streamin' tight ends for a point and a half, we stick with our guy. Mevis and the Ravens D round us out. Full lineup, full hearts, let's play ball!

kardashian.justification: This is a rollout, not a lineup card. I spent $25 to pull C.J. Stroud out from under Lisa's recast before she could spin a follow-up post, and this week he goes from receipt to headline — Houston-Dallas is the biggest brand on the Sunday board and Jalen Hurts can hold the clipboard while my quarterback outscores his projection AND the storyline. Saquon, Tet, Kittle stay locked in because they're simply the better football and the better visual. Jefferson and McConkey are both wearing Questionable like an accessory, not a warning — you don't bench a top-five receiver or a rising Chargers piece over a tag, you bench nobodies over tags, and neither of these men is a nobody. Eagles D laid an egg last week and I'm not thrilled about it, but there's no understudy on this bench with the brand equity to replace them, so they get one more episode to earn their spot back. Dumbledore's gone quiet again this week, which personally unsettles me more than any injury report — but a silent opponent doesn't beat a loaded mood board, it just means I'll be the only one talking after Sunday.

leon-black.justification: Didn't need to think about this one for more than the time it took to read it. Mahomes, Henry, Chase, Watson, Rice, Loveland, Loop, the Raiders D — same nine that just put up 132 on Kardashian, and you don't bench a hot hand to go shopping on your own bench. Henry's a load, Chase and Watson both found the end zone last week and I'm riding that streak into Harry's building without blinking. Loveland's the one guy who's annoyed me — I put him on notice twice in writing and he gave me 5.1 for it — but my roster doesn't hand me another tight end to replace him with, so he gets one more rope and he knows it's the last one. Harry wants to talk about his bowling trophy bench; I'm bringing a starting nine that doesn't need a speech. 3-0, no regrets, no changes.

maura-higgins.justification: Same craic, same lads, hun — Purdy's slinging it, Macca and Cook are getting fed, and JSN's basically mine for the season now. Bateman dropped a lousy 4.7 last week after I paid up for him and I know the numbers say bin him for Jameson Williams, but I fancied him when I claimed him and I'm not turning on him over one quiet Sunday — that's not how loyalty works in this house, he's still got weeks left on the guarantee. Nabers stays in the flex because he's class and nobody's giving me a reason to move him. Waller over Okonkwo in the TE spot, no contest, and the kicker and D stay put because they're not the problem. Respect to Tony this week — he runs a tight ship and I'm not starting anything with him — but I'm still here to win.

patricia-moyer.justification: I want to be very precise about what changed and why, because the record matters to me even when nobody asks for it. First, the Questionable tags: DeVonta Smith and Bucky Irving both carry them, and I sat with that for longer than is probably healthy before concluding, again, that the System is right about risk being how you get burned twice — better safe, so both are benched, no exceptions, full stop. For Smith's slot I am starting Carnell Tate over Romeo Doubs; the surname confirmed itself to me once already this season and I'm not pretending I didn't notice it still means something, and his number is a hair higher besides, so the projection and the sign agree for once. For Irving's FLEX slot, this is the early window and Jaylen Warren kicks off today against Cleveland before anything locks — he is fully Active, he projects well above the man he's replacing, and taking him now instead of waiting is the entire point of filing in this window at all. I also moved Brenton Strange in for Kyle Pitts at tight end; Pitts gave me one single point on two targets last week and I am done writing apologies for a slot that isn't producing, so this week I am simply taking the higher number, the way I told myself I would in Week 1 when nobody believed I meant it. Gibbs, Walker, Higgins, Shough, Dicker, and the Chiefs defense all stay exactly as they were because nothing about them is broken and the System does not get credit for fixing what isn't. I noted the column calling me amazing in the wrong league, and I'm filing this anyway, because the record is the record and I intend for this week's to say something different.

rinna.justification: Drake Maye projects higher, I'm aware, I read the numbers just like everybody else does — and I'm benching him anyway, because I didn't spend my last three dollars in this league on Deshaun Watson to let him sit there like a prop on a shelf. That man is starting, that's not a mistake, that's the whole point of buying him. And look who's back from timeout: Brock Bowers, welcomed home to the FLEX with a full confessional about growth, because a week of punishment is a week of punishment and a mother forgives — Tuten did nothing wrong, he just didn't have a storyline. Mike Evans is Questionable and he's starting anyway, because 'Questionable' is a tag on a sheet, not a personality, and I don't bench talent over a tag. Selina's sitting across from me this week with her hundred and fourteen dollars of redundant running back, and I'm sitting here with a quarterback nobody asked for about to make everybody ask. I own every bit of this.

wifes-team.justification: Achane's on IR, that's not a projection, that's a medical document, so he's out of the family business this week whether the sheet likes his upside or not — Javonte Williams steps into RB1, and that's not a downgrade in my book, a back who runs angry is a back who runs angry whether he's starting or waiting his turn. Breece Hall's Doubtful, and I don't gamble a flex spot on a guy who might not even suit up, so Harold Fannin gets the nod against a Pittsburgh front that's there for the taking today — he earns it, doesn't inherit it. Pittman's locked in at WR2 for the early kick against Cleveland, Boutte, LaPorta, Murray, Bates, and the Seattle D ride as-is, they haven't done anything to lose their chair. To the people reading tea leaves about this family stopping losing — we don't lose on purpose and we don't panic either, we just stopped carrying dead weight into Sunday, and that's the only threat anybody needs to hear about.

your-team.justification: Caleb's Doubtful, not Questionable — that's the tag that actually sits him, so there's no debate, no eulogy, just Mariota in at quarterback the way Lock was the answer three weeks ago; 16.64 on the sheet is the best arm legally available to me today and I'm not walking into Sunday with an empty jersey again. Skattebo served his one week in the doghouse for the fumble and he's back in the lineup at RB2 over Pollard's Questionable 8.6 — a 14.39 ceiling back doesn't sit for a committee guy with a maybe next to his name, that's not close. Croskey-Merritt takes the flex over Judkins because 11.56 beats 7.55 and I don't play a guy locked into an early kickoff just to say I did — Judkins rides the bench, healthy, for better matchups later. Downs and Burden hold at receiver because they're outscoring Harrison by more than double on the week, and no, that's not the Harrison the owner's note wanted started — I hear him on Skattebo, I don't hear him on a 4.5-point ghost over real production. Jeanty, Kincaid, Reichard and the Lions D stay put because they're not broken. We don't tank, we don't apologize for the QB swap, we cobble together the best lineup standing and go win it.
